title: Delete on a picked through edit joins it, as in Premiere
goal: A cut with nothing removed can now be joined back into one piece, but only from the cut's right-click. A Premiere editor picks such a cut and presses Delete, and here that does not join it, so the quickest way they know does nothing they expect. Make Delete on a picked cut with nothing removed join it, the same as Join Through Edit.
notes: From the rough list of queue/audits/2026-10-17-a-cut-with-nothing-removed-can-be-joined-back-in.json: 'Delete on a picked through edit does not join it, as it does in Premiere; the task asked not to change Delete without a card, so it is left as it was.' No card was ever opened, so the gap would sit unseen. Premiere: select a through edit (the dashed edit line) and press Delete to join it. Reuse the Join Through Edit action from task a-cut-with-nothing-removed-can-be-joined-back-in; do not write a second join. Filed by the digest of 2026-10-17.
acceptance: Reproduced first: what Delete and Forward Delete do today with a through edit picked on a video, pasted into this task's log with the walk or steps that show it
With a cut that removed nothing picked, Delete joins the two pieces into one, exactly as Join Through Edit does, in one undo
Delete on a cut where something was removed (a jump cut) keeps doing what it does today
If the cut carries a transition, the runner picks what Delete does the way Premiere does it and logs 'Chose X over Y because Z'

Try path, no flag changed from Next defaults: open the sample recording, press Command K at 4 s, click the cut, press Delete; audit written under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not
